chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'There is no day except that every limb from the limbs of the body pleads to the tongue, saying: I adjure you by Allah that we not be punished because of you.'

key_terms.عُضْوٍ: Limb or organ of the body

ai.seo_question: How do the body's limbs intercede with the tongue to avoid punishment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the holistic nature of moral accountability by personifying the body's limbs as intercessors for the tongue, urging it to speak truthfully to avoid collective punishment. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of the self, where the tongue's speech directly impacts the spiritual state of the entire body. The imagery underscores the practical necessity of guarding one's speech as a primary means of preserving one's overall integrity in daily life.
